text: So how does a team build against heeyID with no SDK?

text: First, why there is no SDK.
prefix: First, why there is no SDK.

text: The teams of the bank build the apps of the bank.

text: An SDK from heeyID would add work before the first release, and a second release train for every app.
prefix: An SDK from heeyID would add work before the first release, and a second release train for every app.

text: I think no SDK is the honest choice for a first release: the contract is the product, and each team owns its own code.

text: So heeyID gives three things.
prefix: So heeyID gives three things.

text: The REST API.
prefix: The REST API.

text: The OpenAPI contract that describes it.
prefix: The OpenAPI contract that describes it.

text: And an integration guide with the rules for the apps.
prefix: And an integration guide with the rules for the apps.

text: The contract describes every call: the path, the request, the answer and the errors.
prefix: The contract describes every call: the path, the request, the answer and the errors.

text: There is one call for each step: start a registration, verify the code, set the password, log in, approve a login, give consent, open a proofing session and renew a session.
prefix: There is one call for each step: start a registration, verify the code, set the password, log in, approve a login, give consent, open a proofing session and renew a session.

text: Each request carries a correlation identifier, and after registration also the device identifier.
prefix: Each request carries a correlation identifier, and after registration also the device identifier.

text: Each error has one shape: a code, a reason key, a message for the customer, and whether a retry is allowed, and after how long.
prefix: Each error has one shape: a code, a reason key, a message for the customer, and whether a retry is allowed, and after how long.

text: The codes are the error outcomes of the requirements, one to one.
prefix: The codes are the error outcomes of the requirements, one to one.

text: So the app of Jasur never reads a sentence to find out what went wrong.
prefix: So the app of Jasur never reads a sentence to find out what went wrong.

text: It reads the code, and shows the message.

text: Then come the SDKs that do exist.

text: The bank adds the MyID SDK and the TAF SDK to the master app, and only to the master app.

text: MyID runs as a native check inside the app.
prefix: MyID runs as a native check inside the app.

text: The backend opens the session, and the customer never leaves the app: no web view, and no web frame.
prefix: The backend opens the session, and the customer never leaves the app: no web view, and no web frame.

text: The MyID credential never goes to the phone.

text: Each app also gets the push SDK of the bank, to receive the wake-up signals.

text: Now the guide.
prefix: Now the guide.

text: Its most important page is a table: what an app can keep, and where.

text: The device identifier, in the storage that the Keychain or the Keystore protects.
prefix: The device identifier, in the storage that the Keychain or the Keystore protects.

text: The refresh token, in the Keychain, or in storage that the Android Keystore protects.

text: The access token and the identity summary, in memory only, until they expire or the app closes.
prefix: The access token and the identity summary, in memory only, until they expire or the app closes.

text: An approval request, in memory and on the screen, until Aziz answers it.

text: The push token.
prefix: The push token.

text: The app PIN, only as a slow, salted hash, on the device.

text: Then the other column: what an app never keeps.

text: The MyID credential.

text: The MyID result code, after its one upload.

text: A one-time code, after Aziz types it.

text: A limit that the gateway uses.

text: The row about limits matters.

text: But the platform applies every limit itself, on the server.

text: A limit in the app is only a convenience, never a control.

text: Now be honest about the edge of this design.

text: heeyID cannot enforce these rules inside an app.
